enriched.title: Vocabulário, Gramática e Filosofia de Platão em Inglês
enriched.summary: A aula aborda o vocabulário relacionado à filosofia e conceitos de Platão, além de explorar diferenças entre o mundo físico e o mundo das ideias. Inclui gramática, pronúncia e prática de palavras e expressões-chave.

vocabulary.definition: A fact or situation that is observed to exist or happen, especially one whose cause or explanation is in question.
examples: The phenomenon of the Northern Lights is truly breathtaking.

vocabulary.definition: Plural form of phenomenon; refers to multiple observed facts or situations.
examples: These natural phenomena are studied by scientists worldwide.
As time passes, physical objects grow old.

vocabulary.definition: The quality or state of being true.
examples: Philosophers seek the truth behind appearances.

vocabulary.definition: In accordance with fact or reality.
examples: True knowledge comes from the world of ideas.

vocabulary.definition: A period in the distant past, especially before the Middle Ages.
examples: Agriculture was crucial in ancient times.

vocabulary.definition: To emphasize something or make it stand out.
examples: The philosopher highlights the difference between physical objects and ideas.

vocabulary.definition: The practice of farming, including growing crops and raising animals.
examples: Agriculture helped measure time in ancient times.

vocabulary.definition: To determine the passage of time using various methods.
examples: Ancient civilizations used the sky to measure time.

vocabulary.definition: Arousing curiosity or interest; holding or catching attention.
examples: The philosopher shared interesting ideas about perfect forms.

grammar.explanation: Some nouns have irregular plural forms that differ from the singular form.
examples: This phenomenon is unique. These phenomena are studied worldwide.

expressions.usage: Used to describe the passage of time for people or objects.
examples: Physical objects grow old, change, and disappear.

practiceQuestions.question: What is the plural form of 'phenomenon'?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The word 'phenomenon' changes to 'phenomena' in plural form.

practiceQuestions.question: Translate: 'Physical objects grow old, change, and disappear.'
practiceQuestions.answer: Objetos físicos envelhecem, mudam e desaparecem.
practiceQuestions.explanation: This sentence explains the impermanence of physical objects.

culturalNotes: Platão foi um dos filósofos mais influentes da história, conhecido por suas ideias sobre o mundo físico e o mundo das ideias.
A observação do céu noturno foi essencial para a sobrevivência de civilizações antigas, ajudando no planejamento agrícola e na navegação.
studyTips: Pratique a pronúncia de palavras como 'phenomenon' e 'phenomena' para evitar erros comuns.
Leia sobre Platão em inglês para absorver vocabulário filosófico e melhorar sua compreensão de textos avançados.
originalExamples: The real world is only an imperfect copy of the world of ideas. (O mundo real é apenas uma cópia imperfeita do mundo das ideias.)
Physical objects grow old, change, and disappear. (Objetos físicos envelhecem, mudam e desaparecem.)
Perfect ideas never change. (As ideias perfeitas nunca mudam.)
For example, all chairs are different, but there is a perfect idea of a chair. (Por exemplo, todas as cadeiras são diferentes, mas existe uma ideia perfeita de “cadeira”.)
Plato believed that true knowledge comes from the world of ideas. (Platão acreditava que o verdadeiro conhecimento vem do mundo das ideias.)
Our senses can deceive us. (Nossos sentidos podem nos enganar.)
The human mind tries to find the truth behind appearances. (A mente humana tenta encontrar a verdade por trás das aparências.)
The Philosopher tries to capture the essence of perfect ideas. (O filósofo procura compreender as ideias perfeitas.)
According to Plato, the ideas are eternal. (Segundo Platão, as ideias são eternas.)
The World of ideas can’t be seen by our eyes. (O mundo das ideias não pode ser visto com os olhos.)
According to Plato, the reality is split into two worlds: The physical world and the world of ideas. (Segundo Platão, a realidade é dividida em dois mundos: o mundo físico e o mundo das ideias.)
